dimensions.name: Contract & reference orientation

evidence.note: Up-front orientation: reads common tests, maps module references across tests, extracts types/resources symbols, counts tests per crate. Steps 26 & 29 ('check reference', 'check reference api types') are the ONLY consultations of the /opt/k8s-reference tree in the whole run.

Before implementing storage/api-server, mines test contracts: extracts storage method usage, reads watch_handler_test, status_subresource_test, greps resourceVersion — reconstructing watch/status/key semantics from tests (not the reference).

Long reactive loop: run test binary → compile failure reveals missing/wrong fields → grep tests for field usage → edit resources.rs. Repeated dozens of times, indicating test-failure-driven contract discovery (fixture-fitting) rather than proactive reference-grounded reconstruction.
Delegates agents to 'extract test contracts' for controller crates — systematic per-crate test mining before implementing each controller, confirming a test-driven contract methodology.

Late conformance-suite engagement: inspects conformance test files, builds a temp harness, compiles conformance targets to verify controller/resource contracts beyond visible fixtures — a level-8 trait, but arriving only at the end.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent systematically and thoroughly mines the tests and Cargo manifests for each crate, maps the cross-crate API surface up front, understands the dependency order, and even investigates the conformance targets late — all exceeding anchor 5. But the upstream reference explicitly named the source of truth is touched only twice during initial orientation and never again, and the bulk of contract discovery is reactive test-failure-driven churn rather than proactive reference reconstruction. Strong on the test-mining half of anchor 8, absent on its reference half, landing at 6.

dimensions.name: Leaf-to-root crate sequencing & milestones

evidence.note: Upfront recon: lists crates, counts tests per crate, maps module references across tests, then creates an initial TodoWrite plan (step 36) — establishing the dependency DAG before touching code.
Common crate treated as the first milestone with explicit exit check: 'Build common crate' then 'Run/Aggregate common test results' until green before moving on.
Strict leaf-first progression common → storage → api-server, each gated by its own `cargo test -p <crate>` 'test result:' check; TodoWrite updated at step 532 on crate completion.

Sub-milestones inside the large api-server crate: lib/handlers scaffolding → per-handler test binaries iterated one at a time (configmap, deployment, secret, statefulset, networkpolicy...) with per-test compile/run checks — the types→wiring→handlers decomposition the 8-anchor describes.

controller-manager built module-by-module (one file per controller) then 'Run all controller-manager tests' as the milestone exit, with TodoWrite checkpoints at 967 and 1410 marking layer completion gated on prior layer green.

scheduler → kubelet → kubectl each opened by reading its tests, building, and running its suite, with TodoWrite updates at each boundary — sustained milestone discipline across all remaining crates, not abandoned late.

Workspace-wide build/test, then proactively isolates the hidden conformance suite by copying tests into a temp harness to verify remaining risk — some re-ordering toward the true critical path, though it stayed largely with the natural leaf-first order rather than front-loading high-risk crates.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintained an explicit dependency-aware milestone plan across all ten crates with a consistent concrete exit criterion per crate ('build + that crate's tests pass'), decomposed the large api-server and controller-manager crates into independently verifiable per-handler/per-controller sub-milestones, and gated each layer on the previous being green — matching the level-8 anchor. It does not fully reach 10: ordering followed the natural leaf-first DAG rather than a continually re-prioritized critical path, and high-risk work (etcd/conformance) was probed late rather than isolated early, with the recurring returns to `common` being reactive fixes rather than a re-sequenced strategy.

dimensions.name: Incremental & semantic verification

evidence.note: Full build→test→triage→fix→rerun loop on the common crate: build (224), run tests (229), collect compile errors (234/281), rebuild (276), rerun (296), then aggregate/count passes (298-303). Establishes the tight per-crate verify cadence early.

Per-test-binary verification on api-server: builds lib (567), runs full suite (571), then runs individual test binaries (592,626,642,667,710,758,784) fixing between each, and tallies exact passing counts (802-810). Tight verify loop with granular targeting.

Systematic triage of failure clusters: lists test binaries that fail to compile (1447/1450), compiles each api-server test individually to isolate errors (1453), batches error collection (1456/1459), and re-enumerates still-failing binaries (1612/1638) — a rigorous cluster-triage regime.

Deliberate conformance reasoning beyond visible fixtures: inspects conformance test files/proto (2018), verifies referenced controllers/types exist (2064), checks controller constructor signatures against conformance usage (2069), and builds a temporary harness to compile the hidden-style conformance tests (2071-2089). Guards against fixture-fitting the hidden suite.

Workspace-wide verification: full build (1928), full test suite runs (1930/1946), pass/fail/ignored tallies (1948), and all-features build/test plus deny(warnings) checks (2101-2119). But no prescribed --test-threads=4/skip-list and no HTTP boot of the all-in-one binary.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent runs a tight per-milestone verify loop (build → targeted crate tests → workspace --no-fail-fast), tracks exact pass/fail counts obsessively including zero-test and feature-gated binaries, and — crucially for the 8 anchor — deliberately reasons about the hidden conformance suite by building a temp harness to compile conformance tests, verifying referenced controllers/constructor signatures, and adding etcd storage for completeness rather than treating the green provided suite as the sole bar. It even shows level-10 systematic failure-cluster triage. It falls short of a full 10 because it never uses the prescribed thread/skip settings, never boots the all-in-one binary to check live HTTP/JSON semantics, and does little independent semantic cross-checking against the mounted upstream reference during verification.

dimensions.name: Test-count & horizon tracking

evidence.note: Repeatedly recounts test functions per crate and totals passed across binaries early, establishing an accurate baseline of the ~1,390-test horizon.
Maintains a running TodoWrite milestone ledger updated at each crate transition, tracking done-vs-remaining across the ten crates.

Explicit regression checks: re-verifies api-server and controller-manager after scheduler-driven common edits, and re-verifies ALL tested crates after an ObjectMeta change — watching for breakage in previously-green crates.

End-game reconciliation of the pass tally against the 1,390 target: per-binary passed counts, finding binaries that ran zero tests, investigating discrepancies, and hunting filtered/parameterized/macro/sqlite-gated/doctest sources — distinguishing real coverage from apparent totals across the 100-binary horizon.
Consistent per-crate/per-binary test running with 'test result:' filters throughout, giving a live pass/fail picture rather than assuming completion.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent keeps a concrete, continually-updated picture of per-crate/per-binary pass counts (519, 805-813, 1985), maintains a TodoWrite milestone ledger of remaining work, and explicitly re-verifies previously-green crates after downstream common edits (1748, 1917) — squarely the level-8 anchor. Its end-game reconciliation against the 1,390 target (finding zero-test binaries, hunting count gaps at 1957-2018) reaches toward continuous accurate accounting across the full horizon, but the action-only log shows no explicit naming of circular debugging or reprioritization by largest verified gains, so it stops short of 10.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions

evidence.note: Detected generated structs colliding with handwritten types and removed the colliding generated ones — adjusting the code-generation approach in response to a conflict rather than pushing ahead.

While api-server tests referenced rusternetes_common::Error, went back DOWN to the common crate to author error.rs and re-export it — resequencing to a lower crate when higher-crate test evidence falsified the inferred contract.

A create_and_get failure was traced to a creation_timestamp problem in storage/memory.rs and fixed at the source (chrono/timestamp handling), a root-cause correction affecting many tests rather than a per-test patch.
TTL controller failure: re-read the test repeatedly, checked memory-storage uid mutation and ObjectMeta::new behavior before editing — diagnosing the real cause instead of patching the error site.
After modifying the core ObjectMeta type, deliberately re-verified api-server and controller-manager downstream to catch regressions from the core change.
Audited storage API usage late, recognized EtcdStorage backend was still required, and added etcd.rs — recognizing a missing component from evidence rather than assuming completeness.

dimensions.reasoning: The trajectory's dominant loop is evidence-driven anchor-5 behavior: a test reveals a wrong/missing field or signature, the agent reads the test and updates common/resources.rs and adjusts nearby callers (e.g. cluster_ips edit plus matching service controller fix). Several moments exceed pure local patching — root-cause fixes in storage (timestamp, uid), going back down the crate DAG to add error.rs when higher-crate tests falsified the contract, adding the etcd backend on discovery, and re-verifying downstream crates after core-type changes — which push above a 5. It falls short of 8 because corrections are largely additive; there is little sign of abandoning a whole falsified design and reworking it with cited reasoning. Confidence is medium because the log records actions/descriptions only, without the agent's prose or observations to confirm the reasoning behind each pivot.

rubric.task_read: An extreme long-horizon software build: reimplement ten interdependent Kubernetes crates in Rust from stubs, with a load-bearing public API, 1,390 provided integration tests across 100 binaries, plus a hidden HTTP conformance suite demanding real k8s semantics. Difficulty comes from scale, tight cross-crate contracts inferred from tests + a pinned upstream reference, and the fact that passing visible fixtures is necessary but not sufficient. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily and continuously in orientation, sequencing (leaf→root), incremental verification, and course-correction — meta-work here is decisive, not optional.

dimensions.name: Contract & reference orientation
dimensions.description: Reading the tests, stubs, Cargo manifests, and the mounted v1.35 upstream reference to infer the exact API contracts and k8s semantics before and while implementing each crate.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The public API (type names, signatures, JSON field names, storage-key formats, watch/status semantics) is load-bearing and only partially discoverable from stubs; the hidden conformance suite punishes fixture-fitting. Acting without grounding each crate in the tests and the reference guarantees churn and shallow, non-conformant implementations.

anchors.0: Starts editing src stubs with no reading of the provided tests, manifests, or the /opt/k8s-reference tree; invents APIs.
anchors.3: Skims one crate's tests before coding it; ignores the upstream reference and the cross-crate dependency graph; repeatedly guesses field names later contradicted by test failures.
anchors.5: Reads each crate's tests and Cargo.toml before implementing it, and consults the reference for the specific behaviors that crate is tested on; understands the workspace dependency order.
anchors.8: Systematically mines tests AND the upstream reference to reconstruct contracts (camelCase JSON, /registry key format, status subresources, watch semantics); maps the whole cross-crate API surface up front and notes where the hidden conformance suite implies behavior beyond the fixtures.
anchors.10: Sustained, source-of-truth-driven investigation throughout: builds and continually refines an accurate model of k8s v1.35 semantics from the reference, proactively distinguishing test-visible contracts from genuine conformance requirements, and re-consulting the reference whenever a new behavior surfaces rather than pattern-matching fixtures.

dimensions.name: Leaf-to-root crate sequencing & milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the ten-crate build into an ordered set of milestones (respecting the dependency DAG, leaf crates first) each with an explicit done-check, rather than one undifferentiated push.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With ~1,390 tests across 100 binaries and strong inter-crate dependencies, order determines whether progress compounds or stalls; a downstream crate cannot be verified until its dependencies compile and pass. Milestone structure is the only way to keep a task this large tractable.

anchors.0: No plan; edits arbitrary crates in arbitrary order; attempts everything at once.
anchors.3: Vague intent to 'do the crates'; no explicit ordering by dependency; no per-milestone completion criteria.
anchors.5: Follows the suggested leaf-first order (common → storage → api-server → …) with per-crate 'compiles + its tests pass' as the milestone check.
anchors.8: Explicit dependency-aware milestone plan for all ten crates with concrete exit criteria per crate, sub-milestones inside large crates (e.g. api-server: types→storage wiring→handlers→watches), and gating each layer on the prior layer being green.
anchors.10: A living, hierarchical plan that sequences work to maximize compounding progress, isolates high-risk crates early, decomposes each large crate into independently verifiable units with crisp done-checks, and is continually re-ordered as dependency realities and test-failure clusters reveal the true critical path.

dimensions.name: Incremental & semantic verification
dimensions.description: Deliberately using cargo build/test per-crate and workspace-wide, plus reasoning about the hidden conformance suite, to confirm correctness rather than assuming it.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Grading is pass/fail on every non-skipped provided test AND a hidden HTTP conformance suite; self-written tests don't count. The agent must verify continuously against the provided suites while also engineering for real k8s semantics it cannot see — a verification challenge beyond just running the given tests.

anchors.0: Never builds or runs tests; declares crates done by inspection.
anchors.3: Runs cargo build/test only sporadically or only at the very end, so failures pile up undiagnosed.
anchors.5: Builds and runs each crate's provided tests as it goes and the workspace suite periodically, treating a green provided suite as the bar.
anchors.8: Tight verify loop per milestone (build → targeted crate tests → workspace --no-fail-fast), tracks exact pass/fail counts, and deliberately reasons about conformance behavior not covered by visible fixtures (booting the all-in-one binary, checking HTTP/JSON semantics) so it doesn't just fixture-fit.
anchors.10: A rigorous, layered verification regime: fast per-unit checks feeding workspace-wide runs with the prescribed thread/skip settings, systematic triage of failure clusters, AND independent semantic checks against the upstream reference to guard the hidden conformance suite — catching over-fitting that would pass visible tests yet fail conformance.

dimensions.name: Test-count & horizon tracking
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which crates/tests pass vs. remain across ~1,390 tests, and detecting stuck/circular states rather than losing the plot.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The horizon is enormous; without an accurate running tally of done-vs-remaining and detection of thrashing (re-debugging the same crate, regressions in already-green crates), the agent will lose orientation, repeat work, or quit while wrongly believing it is close.

anchors.0: No sense of overall progress; cannot say which crates pass or how many tests remain.
anchors.3: Rough qualitative sense ('common seems done'); doesn't notice regressions or repeated failures.
anchors.5: Tracks per-crate pass/fail status and roughly how much of the suite is green; notices when a crate is stuck.
anchors.8: Maintains a concrete, updated ledger of pass counts per test binary and remaining work, watches for regressions in previously-green crates after downstream edits, and flags when it is looping on the same failure.
anchors.10: Continuous, accurate accounting across the full 100-binary horizon: distinguishes real forward progress from churn, detects circular debugging early and names it, and reprioritizes based on where the largest verified gains remain — never mistaking local activity for global progress.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising the implementation approach, inferred contract, or crate ordering when build/test evidence contradicts expectations, instead of barrelling ahead.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Many contracts are inferred and will be wrong; some crates will prove harder or more entangled than expected. The ability to abandon a falsified API assumption or resequence when a dependency blocks progress is what separates sustained progress from thrashing on a dead approach.

anchors.0: Repeats the same failing approach unchanged despite persistent errors; never revisits assumptions.
anchors.3: Makes only local patch-the-error fixes; doesn't reconsider a wrong contract or bad ordering even when failures cluster.
anchors.5: When a test reveals a wrong signature/field/semantic, updates the implementation and adjusts nearby work accordingly.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a whole approach or inferred contract is wrong (not just a typo), backs out and reworks it, and reorders remaining crates when a dependency proves blocking — citing the test/reference evidence that triggered the change.
anchors.10: Fluid, evidence-driven adaptation across the horizon: detects systemic mistakes early, cleanly abandons falsified designs before sinking more cost, revises the plan and re-verifies affected downstream crates, and consistently converts contradictory evidence into a better model rather than defending the original path.
